tier_reason: Enricher (2026-10-12): no measurement supports the fastring/fastream claim. v3.0.2 test/fast.cc times only the u64toa/u64toh/dtoa primitives (4-digit inputs on the single-table-lookup branch; dtoa against snprintf %.7g on one value with different output), and test/str.cc assigns an empty string in over 90% of its 100,000 timed iterations; no published results, no repetition. No valid measurement.

Enricher (2026-10-12): first-party numbers exist after all. Issue #13 carries the maintainer's 2016-12-31 run (i7 3.40 GHz, Windows 10 x64, VS2015 /O2, 16 rounds of insert-then-erase): std::unordered_map vs etl::unordered_map 10k 26 vs 4 ms, 100k 437 vs 41, 1M 6,386 vs 420, 10M 88,020 vs 4,096 (about 21x), measured on pre-release pool code with an identity hash on sequential keys, a pre-sized ETL map and a single timing; the harness no longer builds and the exact CPU model is not given, so C rather than A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Issue #13 (maintainer, 2016-12-31, i7 3.40 GHz, VS2015 /O2, 16 rounds insert-then-erase): std::unordered_map vs etl::unordered_map 10k 26 vs 4 ms, 100k 437 vs 41, 1M 6,386 vs 420, 10M 88,020 vs 4,096 (about 21x); an earlier third-party bx run had ETL slowest (9,690 vs STL 3,573) before the pool rewrite of February 2017
corrections.caveats: Identity etl::hash<uint64_t> on sequential keys (one key per bucket, best case); ETL map pre-sized while std rehashes in round 1; one timing each; pre-release pool code; harness no longer builds; erase in the last bucket rescans from the first (O(N^2) descending erase); push_back unchecked unless ETL_CHECK_PUSH_POP; full insert without exceptions dereferences a null pool node in NDEBUG builds

tier_reason: Enricher (2026-10-12): the independent Ankerl map_benchmark run is fully reproducible: tools/build.sh with g++-8 Release, CMakeLists at 512810d sets -O3 -march=native C++14, runs were pinned with taskset on an isolated core of a 6C/12T 4.6 GHz CPU, and the all.txt rows recompute to a 1.31x geomean over 56 of 63 rows with result checksums identical to std; the CPU is named (i7-8700) only in a search snippet, which is the one residual gap.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Ankerl map_benchmark all.txt (independent, g++-8 -O3 -march=native, taskset-isolated core): geomean 1.31x over std::unordered_map across 56 of 63 rows, result checksums identical; EASTL's own find_as/char* rows (3.70x VC7.1, 12.49x STLport Debug, 1.04x STLport Release find) compare against a baseline that builds a temporary std::string per lookup
corrections.caveats: First-party find_as rows pit a c_str lookup against std::string construction; uint32 rows use different default hashes; reserve() always rehashes and can shrink buckets (issue #521); CPU name snippet-only
